thread:
Jordan (customer): Hey team — we're seeing intermittent 400s from the embeddings endpoint when we batch requests. Only happens under load (bursting to ~500 qps). Example error: `InvalidInput: dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1537`. Not all requests fail, maybe 1-3% fail in spikes.

Maya (support): Sorry you're hitting this, Jordan. Can you paste a minimal repro or the request payload header/body (anonymized)? Also which client lib and model id?

Jordan (customer): Using our Go client that wraps Redwood API. Model is `open-embedding-1-large` (customer-ported open model). We batch up to 128 by default and use dynamic batching on our side — sometimes we coalesce tiny requests. Here's the request body we send when it fails (snip, sanitized):

```json
{"input":[[0.1,0.2,...,0.0],[0.3,0.4,...,0.0]], "model":"open-embedding-1-large"}
```

We log the vector lengths before sending — they look consistent (1536). But the server complains 1537. Trying to figure out if padding or concat edge-case is adding a stray element.

Liam (eng-runtime): Interesting. A few things to check: 1) Are you doing any serialization that could add a trailing comma or null? 2) Do you ever mix different embedding dims in the same batch (e.g., a legacy model with 1537)? 3) We have a known edge case where dynamic batching + pad-to-multiple handling could miscompute padding length if a request declares shape metadata and a tiny race happens during coalesce.

Jordan (customer): Not aware of mixing dims — all inputs go through same preprocessing. We don't attach shape metadata explicitly. We do sometimes send singletons (1-length batch) and let our client join them into larger batches.

Maya (support): Can you share a raw failing payload log entry (base64 of body ok) and the exact timestamp? We'll correlate with server logs.

Jordan (customer): Sure — one failing request at `2025-12-11T15:04:12Z` (ts 1733915052). Payload base64: `W3swLjEsMC4yfSx7MC4zLDB9XQ==` (really small case to reproduce). Error from API: `{"error":"InvalidInput","message":"dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1537"}`.

ops-bot: Alert: batch-coalescer-v2 reported 1 shape-consistency warning at 2025-12-11T15:04:12Z (trace id: a73b9d)

Liam (eng-runtime): Got the trace id — pulling logs. (a few minutes) I see the batch coalescer received three requests simultaneously. One was a single-element request that had a trailing null in the JSON after our internal normalization step — likely due to our client lib's pointer encoding for sparse vectors. That null became a NaN/extra element after parsing in the C++ runtime, bumping length to 1537.

Jordan (customer): Ah, we do have a small helper that constructs slices with `append` from a pointer and sometimes there is an extra zero value when capacity is mis-sized. But we only saw zeros, not null. How is a null becoming an extra element server-side?

Liam (eng-runtime): When dynamic batching concatenates payloads, the coalescer uses array length reported by the client's JSON array. If there's a trailing comma or if the JSON codec emits `null` for uninitialized floats, our parser can interpret that as an explicit element. In C++/simd path, a `null` maps to 0.0 but still counts toward dimension. So you get an off-by-one.

Eva (oncall): Quick mitigation steps: 1) set your client to send smaller max_batch_size (e.g., 32) temporarily and disable client-side coalescing so server batching handles it deterministically; 2) or add validation on your side to assert len(vector)==1536 before enqueue. We'll also add a runtime guard to reject batches with inconsistent dims before coalescing.

Jordan (customer): Will try now — how to disable coalescing on server side? Is there a flag in the request?

Maya (support): Server-side flags are internal for now. If you set `max_batch_size=32` on your client you can avoid large coalesced merges. Also include `X-Request-Id` header with trace id so we can match.

Jordan (customer): Ok changed to max_batch_size 32 and enabled an assertion. Replaying load — will report.

(10m later)

Jordan (customer): Update: after switching to 32, the 400s disappeared in the first 30m stress run. No more dimension mismatch.

Liam (eng-runtime): Thanks — that confirms it's a coalescing edge. We ran the coalescer unit tests and found a race in the buffer compaction when multiple goroutines push arrays and one push had a `nil` element slice. We'll patch the coalescer to sanitize nulls and add a pre-coalesce shape check. PR incoming.

Maya (support): Jordan — we'll coordinate a non-peak maintenance window for the patch. ETA for deploy: 3 hours. If you want, we can also whitelist your org for a canary so you get the patched coalescer early.

Jordan (customer): Canary would be great — our app is time-sensitive. Thanks.

ops-bot: Deploy job started for coalescer-sanitize (canary) — build bld-2219 — triggered by Liam — 2025-12-11T18:02:00Z

Eva (oncall): After deploy, we'll monitor tail latency and 4xx rates for your org for 6 hours. Jordan — do you still observe any tail latency spikes when batching? We saw earlier that large batches had occasional >2s tail latency due to packing overhead.

Jordan (customer): Good question — yes we saw a few tail spikes (~2.3s) when coalescing batches >96. But after dropping to 32 spikes went away. Are there server-side knobs to improve tail latency without reducing batch size that much?

Liam (eng-runtime): We're evaluating two fixes: 1) coalescer parallel packer to reduce blocking when composing large batches, 2) adaptive max batch size per model that caps at the point where P99 token (embedding vector) time stays within SLO. For embeddings, packing is CPU-bound on pre-processing; parallel packer should improve tail latency substantially.

Maya (support): Short-term: try setting `batch_timeout_ms=10` on your client so the client doesn't wait too long to fill a huge batch. That usually reduces tail. Also ensure `pad_to_multiple_of` is off for embeddings (not necessary) — that avoids extra padding math.

Jordan (customer): Thanks — we'll try batch_timeout_ms=10 and leave max_batch_size=32 for now and request canary.

Liam (eng-runtime): PR merged to canary and rollout started. Patch includes: sanitize nulls in coalescer, reject inconsistent dims pre-coalesce, metrics for "dropped_nulls" and "shape_mismatch_rejects".

ops-bot: Canary deploy finished for coalescer-sanitize (canary) — 2025-12-11T18:23:12Z — build bld-2219 — status: success

(1h later)

Jordan (customer): Canary looks good on our side — no 4xxs and tail latency P99 dropped from 2.3s to 0.9s for batched workloads. Thanks everyone, this was fast.

Maya (support): Great — we'll schedule a full rollout tomorrow during low traffic. We'll also send a short doc with recommended client settings: max_batch_size=32-64 (per-model tuned), batch_timeout_ms=5-20ms, assert vector length server-side before send.

Liam (eng-runtime): Follow-up action items: (1) full roll-out of coalescer-sanitize, (2) add a server-side pre-coalesce reject with clear error text (instead of generic dimension mismatch), (3) add a devex note about client JSON encoding pitfalls for embeddings, (4) instrument coalescer metrics.

Eva (oncall): I'll own the rollout and postmortem notes. Jordan — if you want auto-notify when full rollout completes I can add your org to the canary watchers.

Jordan (customer): Please do. Appreciate the quick help. :thumbsup:

Maya (support): Marking this thread resolved for now; reopen if you see regressions.

Jordan (customer): Will do. Thanks all.

-- end of thread --
